title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: From a polished statue toe to a winter bonfire, these documented Drexel rituals mark exams, arrivals, celebrations, and graduation.

cards.title: Rub the Toe Before the Test
cards.subtitle: Drexel’s bronze good-luck ritual
cards.notes: The promised luck is campus folklore, not a guaranteed outcome.
cards.short_summary: Students have long rubbed the Water Boy statue’s gleaming left toe before exams and other challenges.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel documents a long-running student superstition of rubbing the Water Boy statue’s left toe for luck before exams and other challenges.
cards.source_title: Old Traditions for Drexel’s New Year
cards.access_notes: The statue is inside Main Building, so building access rules apply.

cards.title: A Fight Song Preserved in Print
cards.subtitle: Written by two Dragons in the 1930s
cards.notes: An official recording and sheet music are available online.
cards.short_summary: Gay V. Piercy ’39 and Todd Groo ’41 created the song that entered Drexel’s athletic record in 1938.
cards.evidence_claim: Gay V. Piercy ’39 and Todd Groo ’41 wrote the Drexel Fight Song, which first appeared in the October 1938 Drexel Athletic News.
cards.access_notes: The song and supporting historical material can be accessed through Drexel’s website.

cards.title: Homecoming, but in Winter
cards.subtitle: Drexel moves the familiar fall ritual to January
cards.notes: Individual activities, dates, and eligibility can vary each year.
cards.short_summary: Drexel’s weeklong winter Homecoming gathers students, employees, and alumni for spirit events and athletics.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel holds Homecoming as a weeklong winter tradition bringing students, employees, and alumni together around school-spirit activities.
cards.access_notes: Consult the current Homecoming program for event-specific venues, eligibility, and ticketing.

cards.title: Light the Winter Bonfire
cards.subtitle: Hot cocoa and music open Homecoming
cards.notes: This is an organized University event, not an invitation to create an independent fire.
cards.short_summary: Drexel begins its documented Homecoming sequence with a supervised bonfire gathering on Lancaster Walk.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel’s documented Homecoming sequence begins with a bonfire on Lancaster Walk accompanied by hot cocoa and music.
cards.source_title: Traditions Through the Eyes of Dragons
cards.access_notes: Attend only through the official event and follow its barriers and fire-safety directions.

cards.title: A Pillar Tradition in Drag
cards.subtitle: Drexel Pride Month’s recurring stage event
cards.notes: The event centers performance, satire, community, and challenges to social norms.
cards.short_summary: Campus and invited performers take the stage for a recurring Pride Month celebration open to the Drexel community.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel identifies the Annual Drexel Drag Show as a pillar tradition held during Drexel Pride Month and welcoming the campus community.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the current venue, date, ticketing, and identification requirements.

cards.title: Take Mario’s Yearly Selfie
cards.subtitle: One dragon photo for every year at Drexel
cards.notes: Use the paved area around the artwork and do not climb on the sculpture.
cards.short_summary: Drexel encourages an annual photo with its bronze dragon as a visual record of each college year.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel’s traditions guide encourages students to photograph themselves with Mario the Magnificent each year to document their time at the University.
cards.source_title: Old Traditions for Drexel’s New Year
cards.access_notes: Mario stands outdoors at 33rd and Market streets.

cards.title: DragonFly Takes the Stage
cards.subtitle: A major concert run by students
cards.notes: Artists and event arrangements change between editions.
cards.short_summary: Two student organizations collaborate on DragonFly, a recurring concert series with a long roster of visiting performers.
cards.evidence_claim: DragonFly is a large student-run concert series organized by Drexel’s Campus Activities Board and Dragon Concert Series.
cards.source_title: Traditions Through the Eyes of Dragons
cards.access_notes: Check the current artist, venue, eligibility, and ticket rules for each concert.

cards.title: Start With a Week Before Classes
cards.subtitle: New Dragons arrive through a shared slate of events
cards.notes: Programming changes, so examples from one year should not be treated as a permanent schedule.
cards.short_summary: Incoming first-year and transfer students spend a full pre-class week meeting one another and learning the campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel describes Welcome Week as a full week before classes when new first-year and transfer students spend time together through celebratory and informational programming.
cards.access_notes: Participation details and locations depend on the current Welcome Week schedule.

cards.entity_name: Franklin Institute Welcome Week class photo
cards.title: Meet the Class on the Museum Steps
cards.subtitle: A Drexel banner frames the Welcome Week photo
cards.notes: The source documents the tradition and its 2024 occurrence, not a permanent annual time or location guarantee.
cards.short_summary: New Dragons gather at the Franklin Institute steps during Welcome Week for a class photograph with the Drexel banner.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel’s 2024 traditions guide identifies taking a picture of the Drexel banner at the Franklin Institute steps during Welcome Week as a time-honored tradition and class-photo moment.
cards.source_title: Old Traditions for Drexel’s New Year
cards.access_notes: Use the official Welcome Week schedule to verify whether and where the class photo will occur.

cards.title: Toast the New Alumni in the Great Court
cards.subtitle: A graduation ritual inside Main Building
cards.notes: The cited account documents the commencement-season practice without establishing a fixed future schedule.
cards.short_summary: Graduating seniors gather in Main Building’s Great Court for the president’s welcome into Drexel’s alumni community.
cards.evidence_claim: Drexel’s traditions account says the President’s Toast takes place in Main Building’s Great Court and welcomes graduating seniors into the alumni community.
cards.source_title: Traditions Through the Eyes of Dragons
cards.access_notes: Attendance and access depend on the applicable commencement schedule and invitation details.
